tweets.text:
Dr. Ahmad Shahidov meets with H E Sultan bin Hassan Al Jamali in Doha

On May 27-28, 2025, within the framework of the international conference titled “artificial intelligence and human rights: opportunities, risks and a vision for a better future” held in Doha, the capital of Qatar, human rights defender and Head of the Azerbaijan Institute for Democracy and Human Rights, Dr. Ahmad Shahidov, met with H E Sultan bin Hassan Al Jamali, the Secretary-General of the National Human Rights Committee of Qatar.

During the meeting, Dr. Ahmad Shahidov expressed his gratitude to the National Human Rights Committee of Qatar for organizing such a prestigious international event and emphasized the importance of discussing the challenges and opportunities brought by artificial intelligence technologies in the field of human rights on an international platform.

In their conversation, the parties discussed strengthening international cooperation in the field of human rights, establishing legal and ethical frameworks for the application of artificial intelligence, and the possibilities of implementing joint projects. Sultan bin Hassan Al Jamali praised Dr. Ahmad Shahidov’s work on international platforms and highlighted the importance of mutual cooperation.

During the meeting, Dr. Ahmad Shahidov presented a special award on behalf of the Azerbaijan Institute for Democracy and Human Rights to Sultan bin Hassan Al Jamali for his contributions to the protection of human rights at the international level. Sultan bin Hassan Al Jamali expressed his gratitude for the recognition and expressed hope that their cooperation in the field of human rights would continue in the future. @QATARNHRC

tweets.text:
"We will just fall short of 2030 to achieve AGI, and it’ll take a bit longer." - Sundar Pichai, CEO of Google and Alphabet

MUST LISTEN to the most realistic explanation of when will we get to AGI.

He talks about how we are in phase of Artificial Jagged Intelligence (AJI) a term probably coined by Andrej Karpathy. This essentially means that we do see tremendous progress in AI and what it can do and then we can trivially find it makes numerical errors or counting R’s in strawberry.

The line of what AGI means is constantly shifting.  We do see glimpses of immense potential like a Waymo or Project Astra in Gemini Live but the term really doesn’t matter. What we know is by 2030 there’ll be such dramatic progress that we'll be dealing with the consequences of that progress, both the positive externalities and the negative externalities that come with it in a big way.

Sundar didn't shy to accept that we will just fall short of 2030 to achieve AGI, and it’ll take a bit longer. 

I agree with Sundar's take. We have indeed come far from recognizing a picture of a cat and identifying it. We should stop worrying about which year AGI will be achieved and enjoy the journey. 

Thanks Lex Fridman for an amazing interview.
